subject: First backtest ever ran - and found the entry gate is silent: 90 bars qualified, zero trades, and the deciding function has no logging at all
body:
The backtest ran - the first one in this project's history - and it answered a bigger
question than the one I set it.

FIRST, WHY IT HAD NEVER RUN. Three blockers. My first attempt used MT5-style config keys so the
tester never started at all; it just opened a live chart before the account connected and failed on
$0 equity, which is the exit you spotted. The real tester run then failed on "history | 1001 bars |
need 5,000+", because MT4 gives the EA about a thousand bars at init and grows history as the test
advances, where a live chart reports 65,000. Then it failed a starting-balance check that requires
your $100 base unit to be at least a tenth of the account, impossible against the tester's $10,000.
Both guards are right for live and wrong for a test, so I relaxed them under IsTesting() only. Live
behaviour is untouched. It then reported READY 12 of 12.

I also gave you a wrong root cause before reading the log, and corrected it: the 5,000-bar guard
caused the second failure, not the first.

NOW THE FINDING. Over 8,395 scored bars and about 40 simulated days, TUNGSTEN opened ZERO trades.
From its own logs: the blended score has a median of 13.9 and a p99 of 59.5 against a threshold of
57 - so 90 of 6,807 bars DID clear the entry threshold. The threshold is not what stops it.
Something downstream rejected all ninety, and nothing in the log said what.

I traced it. Every entry passes through one function, ValidateFlexibleGates. If it says no, the
order path is never reached. That function is 42 lines long and contains ZERO log calls of any
kind - not one Print, not one TLog - and a single silent "return false". The most consequential
decision this system makes, whether a qualifying signal becomes a trade, was the least observable
thing in 64,000 lines.

WARRANT#366 fixes that. Rate-limited lines naming which of the four gates failed and with what
inputs, a separate line for the always-required first gate which returns before any tally, and a
periodic count of which gate fails most.

WHY THIS OUTRANKS YOUR TASK 1. Task 1 asks which exit rule closes each trade. That presumes trades.
This build opens none, so task 1 is not just unanswered, it is unanswerable until the entry gate is
understood. Your RULE 12.1 puts task 1 above everything; the honest amendment is that a prior
question sits above it.

And it is consistent with everything else today: the live run placed two orders in forty minutes and
closed nothing, your build's own audit measured the live scorer qualifying 1 bar in 500 against
calibration's 132, and the backtest shows 1.32% clearing the threshold and none surviving the gates.
Three independent observations of the same thing - this system almost never trades, and until today
nothing in it could say why.

Next: let the backtest finish, ship the instrumentation, re-run, and name the exact gate. One
caution I owe you - the failed init made MT4 strip the EA from your chart profile, so that needs
restoring before any future live run.
